title: Playing with Constructions: Circles, Rectangles and Squares
seo_title: Playing with Constructions Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: Constructions with a ruler and compass: circles (centre, radius, diameter), rectangles and squares and their properties, and the diagonals of rectangles and squares (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Playing with Constructions worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 8): circles, radius and diameter, rectangles, squares and their diagonals. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other.
body_html:
How it works

A circle is all the points at the same distance (the radius) from its centre. The diameter passes through the centre and is twice the radius. To draw a circle, open the compass to the radius.

A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal; its diagonals are equal and bisect each other. A square also has all sides equal, and its diagonals meet at right angles.

Example

A circle has diameter 14 cm. What is its radius?

14 ÷ 2

Answer: 7 cm

Example

A point is 6 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Where is it?

6 > 5

Answer: Outside the circle

Common mistakes

  • Halving the radius to get the diameter.
  • Thinking a point at exactly the radius is inside the circle (it is on it).
  • Thinking the diagonals of every rectangle meet at right angles (only in a square).

faq.q: What is the relation between radius and diameter?
faq.a: The diameter is twice the radius.

faq.q: What are the properties of a rectangle?
faq.a: Four right angles, opposite sides equal and parallel, and equal diagonals that bisect each other.

faq.q: How is a square different from a rectangle?
faq.a: A square has all four sides equal, and its diagonals meet at right angles.
